thesis: This is a close recommendation on an open position, not a new idea. The uranium long is being abandoned because its best available catalyst was delivered and refused: Google signed a 20-year PPA with Constellation on 2026-10-06 funding uprates at 11 reactors, CCJ traded up to 94.57 intraday on it, and then closed 89.07 the next session — below where the week began. Underneath that, three of the last four quarters missed consensus EPS, two of them by 52.7% and 77.2%, analyst bullish share has fallen 3.9 points over four months, there has been no insider buying in six months, and the stock lags SPY over one, three and six months (-14.1%, -10.4%, -38.1%) with the uranium group itself down 22.3% over six.
key_risk: The risk in closing is that this is the bottom: uranium is a genuine multi-year supply-deficit story and a 2028-2032 reactor-uprate cycle does eventually need fuel, so exiting at 89.07 after a 27% drawdown from the 90-day high of 122.30 could be selling into the exact de-rating the thesis was meant to exploit. This is also a conviction-2 call on thin positive evidence — the evidence I have is almost all negative, and the honest statement is that I am acting on the absence of confirmation rather than on a bearish case for the business.
counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that none of my evidence is about Cameco's contract book, which is long-dated and priced years forward, so quarterly EPS misses against sell-side models are close to meaningless for it, and relative strength over six months is a statement about sentiment rather than about the uranium term price. That case is fair and is why this is a close rather than a short. But a position has to earn its slot, and one whose horizon was wrong by a factor of two on target distance and which cannot be configured to clear its own floor has not.

thesis: A mega-cap staple has been de-rated 28% to a one-year low of 123.47 while its own earnings guidance held: management has reiterated FY2026 EPS of $8.55-8.71, which puts the 123.73 close at roughly 14.3x the midpoint against the low-20s multiple PEP has historically carried. The problem causing the de-rating is specific and locatable rather than diffuse — Frito-Lay North America volume went flat despite price cuts of up to 15% on Lay's and Doritos, PepsiCo Beverages North America volume fell 4% (the steepest since Q2 2020), and core operating margin contracted 40bps in Q2 — while the international segments posted solid gains. That is the shape of a fixable regional execution problem priced as a terminal one, which is what the long_term lane is for. The multiple compressed; the earnings did not.
key_risk: The specific risk is that the volume decline is not a pricing problem at all. PEP already cut prices up to 15% and volume did not respond, which says the issue may be demand for the category rather than its cost — GLP-1 adoption and a durable shift away from salty snacks and sugared drinks would make 14.3x the new fair multiple rather than a discount, and the earnings base would then follow volume down. Sentiment confirms the risk rather than the opportunity: analyst bullish share is only 40.0% and fell 4.8 points over four months (strong buys 3 to 2, holds 15 to 17), JPMorgan cut to Neutral from Overweight and Deutsche Bank to Hold from Buy, both citing North America, and there has been no open-market insider buying in six months. Note also the correlation: KHC is already an open staples long in this book, so this is the second bet on the same de-rated-packaged-food driver and should be sized as such.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that I am buying the one thing that has not yet broken — the earnings line — in a company where every underlying volume metric is negative, and that two sell-side downgrades inside a week usually front-run an estimate cut rather than mark a bottom. I cannot answer that with evidence today, which is exactly why the recommendation is to wait for this morning's print rather than to buy the low. If guidance comes down below the $8.55 floor, the valuation anchor this idea rests on moves and the idea is void, not cheaper.
